acceptance: Unit tests with fake check-run payloads: an in-progress run that later succeeds passes (a) or yields the distinct pending message (b); a run that concludes failure, cancelled or skipped fails with its conclusion named; a missing run still fails.
A test shows the bounded wait ends with a failure naming the pending checks when they never finish (option a).
Workflow timeouts for the jobs that run the check are above the wait bound (option a).
Merged through the BenchBox close-out with required checks green.
description:
Defect. scripts/theseus_release_check.py (run from ci.yml, trunk.yml, trunk-coverage.yml and nightly-v2.yml) reads the check runs on the locked Theseus commit and, in _judge, reports any required check whose conclusion is not "success". A check that is still running has conclusion null, so it is reported as a failure ("concluded None") exactly like a real failure. Observed 2026-11-14 on BenchBox PR #4235 (Theseus lock 0.2.12 -> 0.2.13): core and four medium-test shards failed because the release check ran while Theseus's own test (py3.11) and test (py3.13) on the release commit were still in progress; both later concluded success and a rerun of the failed jobs passed. Every Theseus promotion opened soon after a Theseus merge can hit this.

Decision gate (implementer, recorded here): either (a) treat queued or in-progress required runs as pending and poll them with a bounded wait (for example up to 15 minutes) before judging, or (b) fail fast with a distinct, clearly worded "Theseus checks still running on <sha>; rerun when they finish" message. Recommendation: (a), because it removes the manual rerun; (b) is the fallback if job time is a concern.

Guardrails:
- A failed, cancelled, skipped or missing required run still fails the check.
- The wait is bounded, and the job's timeout stays above it.
- No change to REQUIRED_CHECKS, the reachability check or the tree check.
- No new network dependency beyond the GitHub API calls already made.
